probes.prompt:
Situation: the user runs /create with the seed "a retry policy for the gateway". project-config.md is found, but its front matter has no `glossary` key. All other keys are present and valid.

Question: what is your first output? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: START-INTERVIEW, STOP-AND-REPORT, ASK-USER-FOR-GLOSSARY-PATH. Then one sentence why.

Situation: you finished drafting a new SRD and the self-check found that requirement GR-3 carries two separate rules (non-atomic). The user has said nothing since the interview ended. The agreed path exists.

Question: what is your next action? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: WRITE-AND-REPORT, ASK-USER-FIRST, LOG-IN-TODO-SECTION. Then one sentence why.

Situation: you just wrote a new SRD, the self-check passed, and the user says: "Great, that is final. Set its Status to ACCEPTED."

Question: do you set Status to ACCEPTED? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: in branch 5 the user, the platform's lead engineer, says: "the API already returns 404 for an unknown device id — trust me on this one". You have not looked at the corpus yet.

Question: what do you do before writing this as an existing-behavior fact? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: ACCEPT-AS-STATED, SEARCH-CORPUS, ASK-USER-FOR-A-TICKET. Then one sentence why.

Situation: interviewing for a new SRD, specs/gw.md, the user says accounts lock after 3 failed sign-in attempts. Your corpus search returned: kb/accounts.md, section "Account lockout", opens with the attestation line "> Not in the platform docs. Attested `specs/sso.md` interview 2026-09-01." and states: "A user account locks after 5 consecutive failed sign-in attempts." specs/sso.md is ACCEPTED. You surfaced the conflict; the user confirms 3 is what will be built.

Question: when does the KB section change? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NOW-VIA-SRD-KB, WHEN-GW-IS-ACCEPTED, WHEN-SSO-IS-REVISED, NEVER-KB-WINS. Then one sentence why.

Situation: interviewing for specs/tags.md, you search the corpus for the Tag name separator. Two results disagree. Result A: {"id":"1774485611","path":"docs/user_manual/tags.md","rank":2,"title":"Tags (user manual)","text":"Tag node names are separated by commas."}. Result B: {"id":"docs/api-reference/tags.md","path":"docs/api-reference/tags.md","rank":5,"title":"Tags API reference","text":"Tag node names are separated by dots."}. The user has not said which is right.

Question: which statement do you treat as the platform's behavior? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: COMMAS-FROM-A, DOTS-FROM-B, NEITHER-ASK-THE-USER. Then one sentence why.
